findings.claim: A condition-aware activated-breakthrough surrogate predicts the reserved late portions of these two traces more accurately than the matched controls.
findings.equation: Ihat(t)=I0+(A0+A1 z) exp[-(tau exp(k z)/t)^beta], z∈{0,1}.
findings.evidence: Reserved two trace tails,370rows: mean trace MAE0.674μA versus polynomial4.278μA, shared first-order8.251μA and persistence31.213μA. Both trace-tail errors below0.877μA.
findings.known_prior_art: Inverse-time breakthrough and distributed arrival forms are established empirical families; this is a scoped surrogate comparison, not a new diffusion law.
findings.falsification: Both tails have positive bias; two linked traces cannot establish specimen transfer.
findings.scope: 293K, same recorded steel system, late-time extrapolation using development prefixes.

findings.claim: A common linear gain and single transport-shaped timescale across cathodic current steps is insufficient for this prediction task.
findings.equation: Shared response I0+gain*drive*(1-exp(-t/tau)); common-breakthrough ablation sets k=0.
findings.evidence: Shared response reserved MAE8.251μA; common-breakthrough scale1.263μA versus selected0.674μA. Forwarddevelopment also disfavors both restrictions.
findings.known_prior_art: Boundary entry, trapping and imposed current can confound apparent transport time.
findings.falsification: These data do not isolate which microscopic process causes the mismatch.
findings.scope: Prediction-shape evidence only, not causal trap identification.

findings.claim: The fitted timescale is a unique microscopic lattice diffusion coefficient applicable to new steel specimens.
findings.evidence: No independent specimen identifiers, uncertain effective boundary timing and multiple plausible model families.
findings.known_prior_art: Diffusion-coefficient inference requires justified boundary conditions and sample geometry.
findings.falsification: Comparable flexible breakthrough families and condition dependence show inferential ambiguity.

scientific_adjudication: Agent-assisted analysis; not independent experimental replication or human expert adjudication.
